summary: Alan John Bayard Wace was an archaeologist and historian educated at Shrewsbury School and Pembroke College under Robert Alexander Neil. He held posts at the British School at Athens (1914–1923), the Victoria and Albert Museum (1924–1934), Cambridge (1934–1944), and Alexandria University (1943–1952).

Alan Lomax was a scholar who pursued studies at St. Mark's School of Texas (~1929–1930), Choate Rosemary Hall (~1930–1932), Harvard University (~1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (~1934–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).

Alan Sponberg, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned his Ph.D. from the University of British Columbia. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and taught religious studies at Stanford University (attested 1988).

Alan Watts worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studying under Christmas Humphreys, D. T. Suzuki, and Sokei-an Sasaki, among others. He was an Episcopal chaplain at Northwestern (1944–1950) and taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957).

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who completed his MA at the University of Edinburgh and his Ph.D. at the University of Pittsburgh. He taught at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became an emeritus professor at the University of Toronto.

Alastair Gornall works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his PhD from the University of Cambridge (~2009–2013), he was a Research Associate at SOAS University of London (~2015) and an Assistant Professor in the Humanities at SUTD (~2016).

Albert Debrunner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ferdinand Sommer, Alfred Körte, Friedrich Leo, and Jacob Wackernagel. He held professorships and posts at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Bern, Jena, and Basel between 1917 and 1949.

Albert Grünwedel was a specialist in Tibetan studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Munich. He held an honorary professorship at Berlin and worked at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1881 to 1921.

Albert Hoefer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin, where he completed his doctorate and Habilitation. He was a professor at the University of Greifswald from circa 1840 until his death in 1883.
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from circa 1925 to 1929. Following his studies, he held a post at Novartis from circa 1929 to 1971.

Albert Lutz is a scholar in Sinology and archaeology who studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker. He served at the Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art from 1982 and as director from 1998 to 2019.

Albert Schweitzer was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied under Wilhelm Deecke and attended Strasbourg, Tübingen, and the German University of Prague. He held an academic post at the University of Strasbourg from circa 1902 to 1913.

Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva (~1889–1893) as a pupil of Ferdinand de Saussure (~1893–1902). He later served on the faculty at the University of Geneva from circa 1939 to 1946.

Albert Thumb was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing his Habilitation at Freiburg. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (1891–1901), University of Marburg (1901), and University of Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Venn Dicey was educated at King's College School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1854–1858). He held appointments at the University of Oxford (1882) and the London School of Economics (~1896–1899).

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He held posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2013) and the University of Arizona, beginning in 2013.

Albion Moonlight Butters is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard, CIHTS, and Columbia University, completing his Ph.D. under Robert Thurman, alongside training under teachers such as Michael Aris, Noel Q. King, and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Albrecht Hanisch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He has served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Stenzler, Lassen, Gildemeister, and Kuhn. He served on the faculty of Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 until 1901.

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and headed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and Nepal Research Centre.
